results.question: What is our overall gross profit margin?
results.sql: SELECT round(sum((l.unit_price * l.quantity - l.line_discount) / 1.1 - v.cost * l.quantity) / nullif(sum((l.unit_price * l.quantity - l.line_discount) / 1.1), 0) * 100, 2) AS overall_gross_profit_margin_pct FROM orders o JOIN order_lines l ON o.order_id = l.order_id JOIN variants v ON l.variant_id = v.variant_id WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' AND v.cost IS NOT NULL
results.answer: Your overall gross profit margin is 58.32% for the period from October 1, 2025, to September 30, 2026. This figure is based on all available sales data while excluding voided orders and variants that were missing cost data.
results.assumptions: Interpreting as: overall gross profit margin for all data (2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30), excluding voided orders and variants with missing cost data.

results.question: What are our top 5 products by gross profit?

results.question: What is our net revenue after refunds?
results.sql: WITH gross AS (SELECT sum(total) AS gross_revenue FROM orders WHERE financial_status <> 'voided'), total_refunds AS (SELECT sum(amount) AS refund_amount FROM refunds) SELECT round(gross.gross_revenue - coalesce(total_refunds.refund_amount, 0), 2) AS net_revenue, round(gross.gross_revenue, 2) AS gross_revenue, round(coalesce(total_refunds.refund_amount, 0), 2) AS total_refunds FROM gross CROSS JOIN total_refunds
results.answer: Your net revenue after refunds is $3,205,298.79, based on a gross revenue of $3,321,930.71 minus $116,631.92 in total refunds. This covers all time from October 1, 2025, to September 30, 2026, and excludes any voided orders.
results.assumptions: Interpreting as: What is our net revenue after refunds across all time (2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30), excluding voided orders?

results.question: What percentage of orders had a refund?
results.sql:
WITH order_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    count(DISTINCT order_id) AS total_valid_orders
  FROM orders
  WHERE financial_status <> 'voided'
), refund_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    count(DISTINCT r.order_id) AS orders_with_refunds
  FROM refunds r
  JOIN orders o USING (order_id)
  WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided'
)
SELECT 
  total_valid_orders,
  orders_with_refunds,
  round(100.0 * orders_with_refunds / total_valid_orders, 2) AS percentage_with_refund
FROM order_stats, refund_stats;
results.answer: Out of 17,340 total orders, 5.7% had at least one refund, translating to 988 orders with refunds. This data covers the period from October 1, 2025, to September 30, 2026, and excludes voided orders from the total count.
results.assumptions: Data covers 2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30. Voided orders are excluded from the total order count. A refund is counted if the order had at least one refund event.

results.question: How did revenue during the EOFY sale (19 June to 5 July 2026) compare to the same number of days immediately before it?
results.sql:
WITH eofy_sales AS (
  SELECT 
    'EOFY Sale (19 Jun - 5 Jul)' AS period,
    COALESCE(SUM(total), 0) AS gross_revenue,
    COUNT(order_id) AS order_count
  FROM orders
  WHERE financial_status <> 'voided'
    AND (created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney')::date >= DATE '2026-06-19'
    AND (created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney')::date <= DATE '2026-07-05'
),
pre_eofy_sales AS (
  SELECT 
    'Pre-EOFY (2 Jun - 18 Jun)' AS period,
    COALESCE(SUM(total), 0) AS gross_revenue,
    COUNT(order_id) AS order_count
  FROM orders
  WHERE financial_status <> 'voided'
    AND (created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney')::date >= DATE '2026-06-02'
    AND (created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney')::date <= DATE '2026-06-18'
)
SELECT * FROM eofy_sales
UNION ALL
SELECT * FROM pre_eofy_sales;
results.answer: Revenue was higher during the EOFY sale at $246,002.91 across 1,240 orders, compared to $186,171.83 across 794 orders in the 17 days right before it. This comparison assumes gross revenue from non-served, non-voided orders over two equal 17-day periods.
results.assumptions: Comparing the 17-day EOFY sale period (19 June 2026 to 5 July 2026) against the immediately preceding 17 days (2 June 2026 to 18 June 2026). Revenue is gross revenue from non-voided orders.

results.question: Compare weekend revenue with weekday revenue.
results.sql:
WITH order_days AS (
  SELECT 
    order_id,
    total,
    CASE 
      WHEN EXTRACT(ISODOW FROM created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney') IN (6, 7) THEN 'Weekend'
      ELSE 'Weekday'
    END AS day_type
  FROM orders
  WHERE financial_status <> 'voided'
)
SELECT 
  day_type AS day_type,
  COUNT(order_id) AS order_count,
  ROUND(SUM(total), 2) AS gross_revenue,
  ROUND(AVG(total), 2) AS average_order_value
FROM order_days
GROUP BY day_type
ORDER BY gross_revenue DESC;
results.answer: Weekdays brought in more total revenue than weekends, generating $2,147,980.22 across 11,153 orders compared to $1,173,950.49 across 6,187 orders on weekends. However, the average order value was fairly similar between the two periods, at $192.59 for weekdays and $189.74 for weekends. These figures cover gross revenue from October 1, 2025, to September 30, 2026, and assume weekends are Saturday and Sunday.
results.assumptions: Data covers 2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30. Revenue is gross revenue (excluding voided orders) attributed to the order date in Australia/Sydney time. Weekends are defined as Saturday and Sunday, weekdays as Monday through Friday.

results.question: What is the best-selling product in each product type?
results.sql: WITH ranked_products AS (    SELECT        lower(p.product_type) AS product_type,        p.title AS product_title,        SUM(ol.quantity) AS units_sold,        SUM(ol.unit_price * ol.quantity - ol.line_discount) AS gross_line_revenue,        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY lower(p.product_type) ORDER BY SUM(ol.quantity) DESC) AS rn    FROM orders o    JOIN order_lines ol ON o.order_id = ol.order_id    JOIN variants v ON ol.variant_id = v.variant_id    JOIN products p ON v.product_id = p.product_id    WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided'      AND p.status <> 'custom'    GROUP BY lower(p.product_type), p.title)SELECT product_type, product_title, units_sold, ROUND(gross_line_revenue, 2) AS gross_line_revenue FROM ranked_products WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY product_type
results.answer: The best-selling products by volume for each type are the One-Piece Swimsuit in swimwear with 4,043 units ($321,895.78), Straw Hat in accessories with 3,619 units ($171,331.88), Linen Wrap Skirt in skirt with 1,804 units ($153,398.16), Shirt Dress in dress with 1,492 units ($224,593.45), Ribbed Tank in top with 1,395 units ($79,554.72), High-Rise Jeans in pants with 1,295 units ($184,912.94), Wool Coat in outerwear with 828 units ($177,259.45), and Merino Crew Jumper in knitwear with 526 units ($78,007.41). This ranking is based on total units sold across all recorded transactions.
results.assumptions: Interpreting as: What is the best-selling product in each product type? Using explicit JOIN conditions instead of USING to ensure compatibility across SQL parsers.

results.question: What percentage of our revenue was refunded?
results.sql:
WITH rev AS ( 
  SELECT COALESCE(SUM(total), 0) AS total_revenue 
  FROM orders 
  WHERE financial_status <> 'voided'
), 
ref AS (
  SELECT COALESCE(SUM(amount), 0) AS total_refunded 
  FROM refunds
)
SELECT 
  ROUND(ref.total_refunded, 2) AS total_refunded,
  ROUND(rev.total_revenue, 2) AS total_revenue,
  ROUND((ref.total_refunded / NULLIF(rev.total_revenue, 0)) * 100, 2) AS refund_percentage
FROM rev, ref
results.answer: Your refunded revenue came to 3.51% between October 1, 2025, and September 30, 2026. During this period, you issued $116,631.92 in refunds against total revenue of $3,321,930.71. This calculation assumes all refund amounts are counted regardless of when the original orders were placed.
results.assumptions: Calculated across all data from 2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30. Revenue uses non-voided orders.total, and refunds uses total refund amounts regardless of when the original order was placed.
